findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be used more than once
findings.body:
The login flow reads `user.backupCodes`, decrypts it, finds the matching index, nulls it out, and writes the re-encrypted blob back. These are separate steps with no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the old ciphertext.

Two concurrent sign-in requests with the same backup code will both read the unmodified list, both pass validation, and both succeed. This breaks the stated guarantee that each code works exactly once.

The last write also overwrites the other, so two different codes used at the same moment can leave one of them still valid.

Fix: make the update conditional on the previous `backupCodes` value (e.g. `updateMany` where `backupCodes` equals the value read, and fail if count is 0), or run it in a serializable transaction.

findings.title: Backup code matching ignores case and whitespace normalization
findings.body:
Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString('hex')`). The input is compared with `indexOf(code.replaceAll('-', ''))`, which is case-sensitive and does not trim.

The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which nudges users toward uppercase. Users who type in uppercase, or paste a code with a trailing space or newline from the downloaded file, get `IncorrectBackupCode` even though the code is valid.

The same problem exists in `disable.ts`. Fix: normalize input with `.trim().toLowerCase()` before comparing.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in request body crashes the handler
findings.body:
`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` is called on whatever value the client sent, as long as it is truthy. A number, object, or array will throw a TypeError and produce an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.

The same pattern appears in the next-auth `authorize` function.

Fix: validate the body, e.g. with zod or a `typeof === 'string'` check.

findings.title: Exhausted backup codes report 'incorrect' instead of 'missing'
findings.body:
Used codes are replaced with `null` in the stored array rather than removed. Once all codes have been used, `user.backupCodes` is still a non-null ciphertext, so the `MissingBackupCodes` branch is never hit.

The user sees 'Backup code is incorrect' instead of being told they have no codes left. The same logic applies in the login `authorize` path.

Fix: treat an array with no non-null entries as missing.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable/resetState
findings.body:
After the TOTP code is verified, 2FA is already enabled on the server and the modal moves to `DisplayBackupCodes`. Only the Close button calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()`.

If the user dismisses the dialog via overlay click or Escape, which goes through `onOpenChange`, the parent never learns 2FA was enabled. The switch can show the wrong state, and the modal keeps `step=DisplayBackupCodes` with stale codes for the next open.

The Blob object URL is also never revoked when the component unmounts.

findings.title: First 2FA test no longer verifies enablement and leaves backup code dialog open
findings.body:
`expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise, which is always truthy, so it checks nothing. The PR acknowledges this with a FIXME but does not fix it.

The test also does not interact with the new backup-codes screen, so it never confirms that 2FA was actually enabled.

Fix: use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` after closing the backup codes dialog.
